chain.label: American Airlines CASS program failed to detect noncompliant maintenance and recurring engine start failures
chain.trigger: Contributing to the accident were deficiencies in American Airlines' Continuing Analysis and Surveillance System (CASS) program.

chain.label: ATSV-air filter not cleaned or inspected in accordance with C check procedures
chain.trigger: American Airlines' maintenance personnel did not clean the accident ATSV-air filter in accordance with its C check cleaning procedures and, therefore, missed an opportunity to identify and replace the damaged filter.

caused_by.evidence: its CASS program did not adequately detect and correct these performance deficiencies before they contributed to an accident

chain.label: Disintegrated ATSV-air filter element with free end cap inside housing
chain.trigger: the filter element of the ATSV-air filter disintegrated, allowing the end cap to become free, which blocked the air flow

caused_by.evidence: As a result, the damage to the air filter went undetected.

chain.label: Intermittent left engine no-start condition, including on the morning of the accident
chain.trigger: Depending on its location over the fitting, the end cap could block the airflow from the ATSV-air filter to the ATSV...causing an intermittent engine no-start condition

caused_by.evidence: the filter element of the ATSV-air filter disintegrated, allowing the end cap to become free, which blocked the air flow and caused the engine no-start condition

chain.label: Maintenance misdiagnosed the no-start, replacing the ATSV six times without resolving it
chain.trigger: maintenance personnel's troubleshooting efforts for the engine no-start condition incorrectly focused on the ATSV and engine start system wiring

caused_by.evidence: the left engine ATSV had been replaced six times during the 12-day period before the accident to address these engine no-start events
the company's maintenance alert system did not recognize the recurring failed engine starts, ATSV replacements, and MEL deferments as a possible serious problem

chain.label: Mechanics used unapproved manual engine-start procedure, prying on the ATSV manual override button
chain.trigger: American Airlines' maintenance personnel repeatedly used an unapproved maintenance procedure, which included using a prying device to push the ATSV manual override button

caused_by.evidence: maintenance personnel instructed the captain to initiate the manual engine-start sequence...while the maintenance personnel manually opened the left engine's air turbine starter valve

chain.label: Bent ATSV manual override internal pin holding the ball valve off its seat
chain.trigger: the internal pin in the left engine ATSV override button was bent

caused_by.evidence: using a prying device to push the ATSV manual override button, to manually start the accident engine, which resulted in bending the internal pin in the override button

chain.label: Uncommanded ATSV opening at takeoff power; air turbine starter freewheeled to catastrophic failure
chain.trigger: resulted in the uncommanded opening of the ATSV during high-power engine conditions at the beginning of the takeoff roll and caused the ATS to freewheel until it sustained a catastrophic internal failure

caused_by.evidence: A bent manual override pin can become stuck and fail to retract fully, preventing the ball valve from sealing completely.

chain.label: Combustible fluid (oil, hydraulic fluid, or fuel) available in the engine nacelle cavity
chain.trigger: a combustible fluid, such as oil, hydraulic fluid, or fuel, was available in the engine; however, fire damage precluded the determination of the specific source

chain.label: In-flight left engine nacelle fire during departure climb
chain.trigger: experienced an in-flight left engine fire during departure climb from Lambert-St. Louis International Airport

caused_by.evidence: the open ATSV and resulting failed ATS allowed a hotter than typical airstream and/or incandescent particles to flow into the engine nacelle area and likely provided the ignition source for the in-flight fire
For a fire to occur in the engine nacelle cavity, an ignition source and a combustible fluid source must have been present.

chain.label: Captain did not allocate tasks; first officer handled ATC radio while running the emergency checklist
chain.trigger: the pilots failed to properly allocate tasks, including checklist execution and radio communications, and they did not effectively manage their workload

caused_by.evidence: After the Left Engine Fire warnings activated, the first officer contacted ATC to report the emergency and the flight's immediate return to STL.

chain.label: Engine Fire/Damage/Separation checklist interrupted for nonessential tasks, delaying fuel shutoff and agent discharge
chain.trigger: a subsequent left engine fire, which was prolonged by the flight crew's interruption of an emergency checklist to perform nonessential tasks

caused_by.evidence: At 1314:49, the first officer began performing the Engine Fire/Damage/Separation checklist.
About 80 percent of the pilots' delay in performing the third item on the checklist...was caused by their performance of tasks unrelated to shutting off fuel to the engine and stabilizing the fire.

chain.label: Prolonged fire caused electrical anomalies and loss of left hydraulic system fluid and right-side pressure
chain.trigger: the airplane began to experience some electrical malfunctions, which resulted in the loss of the captain's primary flight and navigation display panels

caused_by.evidence: the pilots' interruption of the emergency Engine Fire/Damage/Separation checklist at a critical point prolonged the fire and led to additional problems, including the loss of hydraulic pressure
electrical problems resulting from the engine fire caused some instrumentation loss, the illumination of multiple annunicators

chain.label: Nose landing gear failed to extend on approach
chain.trigger: The tower controller reported that the nose landing gear was not extended

caused_by.evidence: the loss of hydraulic pressure, which caused the nose landing gear to fail to extend

chain.label: Go-around, emergency nose gear extension, and emergency landing at STL with substantial fire damage
chain.trigger: the flight crew executed a go-around, during which the crew extended the nose gear using the emergency procedure. The flight crew conducted an emergency landing

caused_by.evidence: the first officer responded that they were going to go around
The captain stated that the flight would need to return to STL, and he then asked the first officer to contact STL and declare an emergency

chain.label: No company guidance or training that opening the pneumatic crossfeed valve retracts the engine fire handle
chain.trigger: American Airlines' manuals and training did not indicate that opening the crossfeed valve causes the fire handle to retract, reversing the shutoff of fuel

chain.label: First officer opened the left pneumatic crossfeed valve on the ground, retracting the fire handle
chain.trigger: the first officer opened the left pneumatic crossfeed valve to improve the airflow in the cabin, which caused the left engine fire handle to retract

caused_by.evidence: the first officer did not have a clear understanding of the relationship between the pneumatic crossfeed handle and the engine fire handle, most likely because of inadequate company guidance and training

chain.label: Fuel reintroduced to the damaged left engine and dumped onto the ground, re-triggering the fire warning
chain.trigger: someone outside of the airplane informing the pilots that the left engine was 'dumping gas'

caused_by.evidence: caused the left engine fire handle to retract and fuel to flow into the damaged engine area. Subsequently, fuel dumped onto the ground.

chain.label: Fire extinguished by ARFF and all 143 occupants deplaned on the runway without injury
chain.trigger: the 2 flight crewmembers, 3 flight attendants, and 138 passengers deplaned on the runway. No occupant injuries were reported, but the airplane sustained substantial damage from the fire.

caused_by.evidence: the captain landed the airplane successfully about 1332. After the airplane stopped on the runway, ARFF personnel applied fire-extinguishing agent to the left engine.
The IC decided to deplane the passengers, which ARFF personnel relayed to the pilots through the cockpit window.
